title: EBE Core Lock v1.0: The S-Dynamic Foundation
description: Specifies the Core Lock dynamical engine for Entropy-Bounded Empiricism (EBE): a running grid-state parameter f(S) with constant negative beta function that uniquely yields an exponential form and a conserved information length. Physical observables project through an accumulated phase Φ(S), producing a proxy-independent, falsifiable prediction that any detected variations in constants must exhibit a constant log–log correlation slope d ln v / d ln c = constant. Current null results constrain couplings but do not falsify the framework absent a specified projection.

beta_constraint.description: Constant negative beta function along the entropy axis S that fixes the running of the grid-state stiffness f(S).

grid_state_solution.description: Unique exponential solution for the grid state function implied by the constant beta constraint.

running_phase.description: Accumulated information length (phase) that drives observable projections.

information_invariant.description: Total information length over the physical domain is an invariant.

projection_law.description: Observable X projects from the hidden phase with coupling coefficient a_X.

correlation_test.description: Proxy-independent prediction: ratios of log-derivatives between any two varying observables are constant.

key_results.main_finding: A constant beta function in S enforces an exponential f(S) and yields a falsifiable, proxy-independent correlation prediction d ln v / d ln c = constant, with current null results constraining couplings but not the engine.
parameters_tested: Constant beta constraint: d ln f/dS = -1/ΔS
Exponential grid state: f(S) = f0 exp(-S/ΔS)
Correlation slope: d ln v / d ln c = a_v/a_c
datasets_used: Analytic derivation (closed-form solution for f and Φ)
Internal numerical verification (simulation of slope stability)
Literature constraints on Δα/α and Δμ/μ (quasar absorption, H2, methanol, JWST)

sealed_predictions.statement: If any variations of fundamental constants are detected, the log–log slope between any two independently varying observables must be constant (d ln v / d ln c = a_v/a_c) across redshift, time, and environment.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint measurements of two or more varying constants across multiple bins (e.g., redshift or time) demonstrating a statistically significant (>3σ) change in the slope d ln v / d ln c or inconsistent slopes across subsets.

sealed_predictions.statement: Any confirmed variation in one constant must be accompanied by co-variation in at least one other independent observable consistent with a single constant slope ratio.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-confidence detection of variation in one constant with simultaneous measurements showing no co-variation in all tested second observables, such that any constant-slope model is excluded at >3σ.

kill_criteria: KC1: Observation of two or more varying constants with a redshift/time/environment-dependent slope d ln v / d ln c that cannot be fit by a single constant ratio (excluded at >5σ after systematics).
KC2: Three or more observables exhibit pairwise slopes that are mutually inconsistent with any single set of constant couplings {a_i} (global constant-ratio fit rejected at >5σ).
KC3: Empirical reconstruction from multi-observable data requires a non-exponential f(S) (i.e., an S-dependent beta function) at high significance, invalidating the constant-β constraint.

KC4: Robust evidence of oscillatory or sign-changing variations in constants across ordered datasets that cannot be produced by a monotonic accumulated phase Φ(S) implied by constant β (excluded by model-independent tests at >5σ).

KC5: Detection of variation in one constant with simultaneous bounds on another that exclude any constant finite slope between them across the same sample (i.e., constant-correlation models ruled out at >5σ).
epistemicStatus: Layer B - Mathematical engine compatible with current null results

equations.correlation_test: d ln v / d ln c = a_v/a_c = constant
